newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge may hold government negotiators.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge may hold government negotiators.

text.p: Military officers were on Sunday trying to secure the freedom of government negotiators who are feared held by Khmer Rouge hardliners in northern Cambodia, an officer said.
Hem Bunheng, a deputy governor of Siem Reap province, was among those on a helicopter that failed to return to base on Saturday, said Prom Sanein, deputy commander of military region number four.
Prom Sanein, reached by telephone in Siem Reap, did not know how many people were missing, and said: "Maybe they were lost so they landed in the wrong place, in Khmer Rouge territory."
He said a military regional commander, General Khan Savoeun, had left on Sunday "to negotiate in order to release them", adding: "Until now we have no information."
The government has been trying to persuade hardline members of the Khmer Rouge to come over to the government.
The Khmer Rouge, whose 1975-79 rule left more than one million people dead, reneged on a 1991 peace pact and fought the coalition government formed after U.N.-run general elections in 1993.
But the movement began falling apart after former top official Ieng Sary split with the hardliners last August.

Thousands of guerrillas have come over to the government side since Ieng Sary won a royal pardon last September from a 1979 death sentence handed down in absentia for his role in the Khmer Rouge's "killing fields" rule.
An estimated 2,000 hardliners are holding out around the northern base of Anlong Veng, and the government has said it wants to win them over with words rather than guns.
The government believes they may be holding Christopher Howes, a British mine clearance supervisor, who was abducted in Siem Reap province in March last year.
He was reported to have escaped last November but never showed up in government territory.
